Rachel / Asha,

Following up with technical detail for Asha's items — high level then attachments to follow:

- Data residency & flows: Production model runtime may be in multiple cloud regions depending on deployment type. For Redwood Hosted API we store model outputs and request metadata in region-specific storage with encryption at rest (AES-256). For Dedicated and Private we can pin workloads to regions and offer VPC routing. See redwood-data-flow-matrix.xlsx (tab: region-mapping).

- Transfer mechanisms: We can execute SCCs (Controller-Processor additions) and have a standard DPA + Annex but will support customer redlines where reasonable. If Silverpine requires DPF-style evidence we will assemble: mapping, technical measures, personnel access controls, subprocessors, incident handling timelines, and a sample audit log extract.

- KMS & keys: Options are:
  * Redwood-managed keys (default): keys stored in cloud KMS, rotated per policy; Redwood holds key material.
  * Customer-managed keys (CMK) in cloud KMS: customer provides key project/ARN and we use it for encryption-at-rest; key material not exported.
  * On-prem HSM (Redwood Private / on-prem deployment): full customer control -- recommended for regulated workloads.

- Access logs & audit: We retain auth/tracing logs for 365 days by default; extended retention is available as an add-on. We can provide redacted sample logs and a runbook for how to request audit exports.

- Subprocessors: We maintain a living subprocessor list and provide 30-day notice for changes; typical subprocessors include cloud providers, monitoring, and observability vendors.

I'll attach a short KMS options doc and a sanitized SOC 2 index for your review. If you need a signed security questionnaire (e.g., SIG Lite) we can return that within 3 business days.

Ben Carter
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
